stem: In a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system, what is the role of embeddings?

options.text: They compress the final answer to save tokens
They map text to vectors so that semantically similar passages can be found by similarity search
They encrypt documents at rest
They decide which user may see a document

explanation: Embeddings place text in a vector space where distance reflects semantic similarity, enabling retrieval of passages relevant to a query even without shared keywords.

stem: A search over product codes and part numbers misses exact matches when using only vector similarity. What is the standard remedy?

options.text: Use a larger embedding model only
Combine keyword (lexical) search with vector search and rerank the merged results
Lower the number of documents indexed
Remove numbers from the documents

explanation: Dense vectors capture meaning but are weak on exact identifiers. Hybrid retrieval adds lexical matching, and a reranker orders the combined candidates by relevance.

stem: A client wants a model to answer from internal documents that change daily and must be traceable to source. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Fine-tune the model weekly on the documents
Retrieval-augmented generation over an indexed, regularly refreshed document store with citations
Paste every document into each prompt
Train a model from scratch

explanation: Fine-tuning bakes knowledge into weights, is slow to refresh and poor at attribution. Retrieval keeps knowledge external, updatable and citable.

stem: A RAG assistant answers well on short FAQs but poorly on long technical manuals. Retrieved chunks often start mid-sentence and answers miss definitions given earlier in the same section.

options.text: Chunk along document structure (headings and sections), keep a small overlap, attach section titles as metadata to each chunk and test retrieval on a set of real questions.
Increase the chunk size to the maximum the embedding model allows.
Switch to a bigger generation model.
Reduce the number of retrieved chunks to one.

rationales.text: Structure-aware chunks keep related definitions and context together.
Generation model size fixes retrieval problems.
Metadata such as section titles helps both retrieval and citation.
Retrieving a single chunk always gives the most precise context.

explanation: Poor chunk boundaries separate context from the text that needs it. Structure-aware chunking with metadata improves retrieval, and evaluating on real questions confirms it. Bigger chunks dilute relevance; a bigger generator cannot use text that was never retrieved.
model_answer: Re-chunk by headings, add overlap and section metadata, consider retrieving parent sections, build a retrieval test set from real questions and compare recall before and after.

rubric.criterion: Adds metadata for context and citation

stem: A support assistant retrieves ten passages per query. Users report relevant answers exist in the knowledge base but the assistant often answers from tangential passages.
constraints: Latency budget allows one extra processing step
A labelled set of 200 question and answer-passage pairs exists

options.text: Retrieve more candidates, add a reranker to order them for the query, and measure recall at k and ranking quality on the labelled set before and after.
Increase k to twenty and pass everything to the model.
Remove overlapping articles at random to reduce noise.
Ask users to rephrase their questions more precisely.

rationales.text: A reranker can promote the truly relevant candidates from a wider pool.
Passing more passages always improves answers.
A labelled set allows objective comparison of retrieval changes.
Users are responsible for query quality.

explanation: The relevant passage is being retrieved but not prioritised. Reranking addresses ordering; retrieval metrics on a labelled set show whether it helped. More context can distract the generator.
model_answer: Widen the candidate pool, add a cross-encoder or similar reranker, evaluate recall@k and ranking metrics on the labelled set, and check latency stays within budget; handle duplicates deliberately rather than randomly.

rubric.criterion: Adds reranking or equivalent ordering step
